headline: The Partnerships and Launches That Came Out of Big 5 Construct Saudi
deck: No headline contract awards. Instead, product debuts, channel expansion, a new integrated FM and fire-safety operation, and three sustainability awards.
excerpt: Big 5 Construct Saudi produced product debuts and channel moves rather than contract awards: Kiwi Information Technology debuted Philips Home Access Solutions, Al-Futtaim launched integrated FM and fire and life safety operations in the Kingdom, and the Impact Trail awards went to PRIMECO, Masdar and Al-Futtaim Engineering.
content:
Big 5 Construct Saudi is a selling show rather than a signing show, and the corporate news that comes out of it looks different from a project conference. There were no headline contract awards announced from the halls at Riyadh Front over the four days. What there was instead is a set of product launches, distribution moves and service-line expansions, most of them aimed at establishing or deepening a Saudi position.

The formal recognitions came through the Big 5 Impact Trail, the show's sustainability award programme, and all three went to companies with operating businesses rather than concepts. Prime Middle East Trading Company, which trades as PRIMECO, took the sustainability innovation award for its work with Honeywell's Solstice low-global-warming-potential refrigerant range. Masdar won best circular economy solution for its Kronospan carbon-negative wood-based panels and engineered boards. Al-Futtaim Engineering Company took the operational sustainability award for an integrated facilities management solution. The Impact Trail also spotlighted work from Galaxy Technology, whose Albion Valves range is exhibited with published carbon data across its cast-iron products, Star Factory in spray polyurethane foam roofing and waterproofing, and Keller in ground improvement and foundations.

The clearest launch of the show came from Kiwi Information Technology Co. Ltd., which used Big 5 Construct Saudi to debut Philips Home Access Solutions in the Kingdom and to expand its channel partnerships across Saudi Arabia. Access control and door hardware is a category where a brand is only as good as the installer and service network behind it, which is why the announcement was about channel depth rather than about the product itself.

On the services side, Al-Futtaim Contracting has launched integrated facilities management and fire and life safety operations in Saudi Arabia, bringing together Al-Futtaim Facilities Management with the fire and life safety division of Al-Futtaim Engineering. It is a structural move rather than a product one: it puts a maintenance business and a regulated safety discipline under a single Saudi contract, at a moment when the Saudi Building Code's fire requirements are enforced through permitting.

Certification arrived as a joint proposition. Eurovent Certita Certification exhibited alongside Eurovent Middle East, the regional arm of the European HVACR industry association, promoting a Desert Certification option for the six GCC markets that tests at 35C and 46C, requires demonstrated operability at 52C and publishes a part-load Desert Seasonal Energy Efficiency Ratio. Bringing a certifier and an industry association to a stand together is a deliberate signal to Saudi consultants that third-party performance data is becoming a specification norm.

Several partnerships on the floor were long-standing rather than new, and worth recording for what they show about how this market is actually served. Haier's Saudi business runs through Haier and Aljabr Saudi Electronics Company, formed with the Al Jabr group and a sponsor of the show. Topwerk's HESS Group concrete plant business operates in the Kingdom through Topwerk Middle East, which has installed lines for Arabian Tile Company and Saudi Pan Kingdom and supplied an expansion at Riyadh Kingdom Concrete Products. Kimmco-Isover, the insulation venture between Alghanim Industries and Saint-Gobain Isover, supplies the region from a stone wool plant at Yanbu and a glass wool factory in Kuwait.

Two things are notable about that list. The first is that almost every move is about the channel, the service network or the certification, and almost none is about a new product category. The second is that the announcements cluster around companies that already have a Saudi entity, which is consistent with what BrentDesk observed about the shift in international manufacturers' questions from how to sell here to how to be here.

The show ran under the patronage of the Ministry of Industry and Mineral Resources and was opened by Eng Fawaz bin Badr Al Shora, Deputy Minister of Industry and Mineral Resources for Industrial Services and Compliance. That patronage is itself a signal about where the ministry wants the industry's commercial announcements to point: at manufacturing and compliance rather than at import volume.
